classification.difficultyReason: Connects the supplied altitude equalities to two area expressions, chooses cross-substitutions to derive the identity, then decomposes 75 degrees into known exact angles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In the diagram, show that $y=a\cos\alpha$ and $y=b\cos\beta$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with B left, A right and C above. The perpendicular from C meets BA internally; its foot is unlabelled in the printed diagram. Alpha and beta label the two apex sectors. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: CB=a, CA=b, altitude=y; alpha is between CB and the altitude, beta between the altitude and CA.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels and the right-angle marker appear.

answer.worked:
In each right-angled triangle, the altitude is adjacent to the marked angle:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=\frac ya\\a\cos\alpha&=y\\\cos\beta&=\frac yb\\b\cos\beta&=y.\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=a\cos\alpha$ and $y=b\cos\beta$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using the formula for the area of a triangle, $\frac12ab\sin C$, prove that $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta$.

answer.short:
$\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta$.

Equate the area of the whole triangle with the sum of the two smaller triangle areas, and substitute part a.
answer.worked:
The whole apex angle is $\alpha+\beta$. The altitude divides the triangle into two triangles, so
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(ABC)&=\frac12ab\sin(\alpha+\beta)\\\operatorname{Area}(ABC)&=\frac12ay\sin\alpha+\frac12by\sin\beta.
\end{align*}$$
Use $y=b\cos\beta$ in the first term and $y=a\cos\alpha$ in the second:
$$\begin{align*}\frac12ab\sin(\alpha+\beta)&=\frac12ab\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\frac12ab\cos\alpha\sin\beta\\\sin(\alpha+\beta)&=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta.
\end{align*}$$
